newsitem.title: EGYPT: Egypt evacuates pregnant Palestinian from camp. [CORRECTED 13:30 GMT]
newsitem.headline: Egypt evacuates pregnant Palestinian from camp. [CORRECTED 13:30 GMT]

text.p: Egypt has evacuated a heavily-pregnant Palestinian, bleeding and in danger of dying, from a desert camp on the border with Libya where she and about 200 others have been stranded for more than a year.
It was the first crack this year in Egypt's refusal to let in any of the refugees from the wasteland camp, described by aid workers as a rubbish dump unfit for human habitation.
"We are really delighted. It is great news and we hope the other medical cases will also be evacuated," said U.N. High Commissioner for Refugees (UNHCR) spokesman Panos Moumtzis.
But he said there were no assurances the woman, who UNHCR officials have said was haemorrhaging and feverish, could remain after treatment.
The refugees were among thousands of Palestinians expelled by Libyan leader Muammar Gaddafi last year to expose what he sees as a hollow peace deal between their leaders and Israel.

Egyptian Defence Minister Field Marshal Mohamed Hussein Tantawi agreed late on Tuesday to let 30-year-old Ferial Ali Mahmoud, who is eight months pregnant, enter Egypt for care on humanitarian grounds.

"She will not be allowed to leave the hospital until the delivery and we are confident that she and the child are healthy," said Nabil al-Shanawani, the director general of health affairs in Marsa Matrouh, about 210 km (125 miles) from the Libyan border.

There are hopes that two other critically-ill refugees, a man suffering from diabetes complications and an eight-year-old girl with a heart defect, will be evacuated next, Moumtzis (corrects from Moumtiz) said.
Most Palestinian deportees from Libya went on to other countries but Egypt has refused to let in those unable to prove they can leave the country by another border.
So far no country has agreed to take the Palestinians.
Moumtzis, who visited the camp last week, said: "These people are feeling fed up and forgotten by the rest of the world."
"The children just chase scorpions and snakes all day. We felt awful leaving the camp. The people were clutching onto us. They want something to happen immediately," he added.
